#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh — sandbox materialisation and arm toggles
#
# cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.6 (SDD D-4.5, DEC-0421, DEC-0423, DEC-0396).
# Extracted from execute-agent.sh (cycle-129 step 2 and the toggle functions)
# WITHOUT behaviour change for the cycle-129 single-skill path, and shared with
# pipeline-run.sh. Source it; it defines functions only and sets no shell
# options (the caller runs under `set -euo pipefail`).
#
# Contract (every function returns 0 on success, 2 when refused / when a step
# cannot take effect; refusals name the reason on one stderr line):
#
#   mount_prompt_surface <ws> <prompt_tree> <skill|->
#       skill given: <ws>/.claude/skills/<skill>/ (whole dir), .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md,
#       .claude/rules/, CLAUDE.md = "@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"; the prompt tree's
#       .loa.config.yaml only in arm mode (LOA_EVAL_ARM set), as cycle-129 did.
#       skill "-": the whole .claude/ tree is copied (files, never a symlink to the
#       tree), CLAUDE.md as above, and .loa.config.yaml always (the pipeline
#       executor needs every skill, hook and script). Evidence: mount=skill:<s>|tree.
#   resolve_arm_toggles <arm> <suite_file>
#       prints the arm's toggles as compact JSON on stdout. Arms are read from
#       `.arms[]` (ablation-2.0) and `.ab.arms[]` (recall suites). An arm with
#       toggles {} (a1_full, baseline) prints {}; `baseline` undeclared prints {}.
#       Exit 2: undeclared arm (an unreadable suite file declares none), `absent: true` arm.
#   apply_arm_toggles <ws> <toggles_json> <arm>
#       applies every toggle to the SANDBOX COPY and verifies it afterwards; exit 2
#       when one cannot take effect or is unknown. Toggles and values:
#         companion_voice: false  flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false
#         karpathy_block: false   '## Karpathy Principles' out of CLAUDE.loa.md (+ constraints.json rows)
#         rule_files: false       stash-safety.md, skill-invariants.md out of .claude/rules/
#         audit_delta_instruction: false  the delta paragraph out of auditing-security/SKILL.md
#         loa_mount: false        verifies no .claude/, CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml in <ws>
#                                 (the caller skips mount_prompt_surface); evidence loa_mount=none
#         effort: low|medium|high|xhigh|max
#                                 every `effort:` line out of the frontmatter of every
#                                 <ws>/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; every `default_effort` key in
#                                 <ws>/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml set to the value and its
#                                 .checksum (bare sha256 hex) refreshed when present.
#                                 The caller passes `--effort <v>` on argv.
#         gates: false            flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.enabled=false;
#                                 LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false exported in the CALLING shell
#                                 and written to $ARM_ENV_FILE (KEY=VALUE lines) when that is set
#         flatline: false         flatline_protocol.enabled=false
#         sprint_plan: false, context_resets: false
#                                 phase-set edits owned by the pipeline executor; recorded as
#                                 evidence here (the single-skill executor refuses them itself)
#   regen_sandbox_manifest <ws>
#       writes <ws>/.claude/checksums.json {generated, algorithm: sha256, files} over
#       every regular file under <ws>/.claude except overrides/ and the manifest
#       itself (LC_ALL=C order, sha256). tools/gen-checksums.sh (in the
#       prompt tree, $EVAL_PROMPT_TREE) is used instead when it exists AND <ws> is a
#       git repository tracking .claude files (it lists `git ls-files`). No .claude/
#       (loa_mount: false) → manifest_sha256=none, exit 0. Prints manifest_sha256=<hex>.
#   check_fixture_path_rule <fixture_dir>
#       exit 2 (offending paths on stderr) when the fixture's top level holds
#       .claude, CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml, grimoires or .run — the mount owns
#       those paths (DEC-0396); exit 0 otherwise.
#   write_sandbox_grimoire <ws> <task_yaml> <arm> <sprint_label>
#       grimoires/loa/ledger.json (one active cycle, <sprint_label> planned, global 1;
#       the ledger-lib.sh schema), NOTES.md (header only), context/task-brief.md (the
#       task's agent-facing `criterion` + the TASK.md next to task.yaml),
#       a2a/<sprint_label>/ (empty); review-catch tasks also get a one-sprint
#       grimoires/loa/sprint.md naming pr/head.diff and a2a/<sprint_label>/reviewer.md
#       carrying pr/PR.md (sandbox copy, else the corpus fixture's). An arm whose
#       toggles carry sprint_plan: false (resolved from $LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE, default
#       evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml) gets NO sprint.md. Build tasks leave sprint.md
#       to the PLAN phase. Nothing written names the arm.
#   init_sandbox_beads <ws> <task_title>
#       `br init --prefix bd --no-daemon` in <ws> plus one task bead with the title
#       when br ($LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN, default br) is on PATH → beads=br; else the opt-out
#       marker through <ws>/.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh --opt-out →
#       beads=opt-out; neither → beads=none (exit 0).
#
# Hashing is Python hashlib (_sm_sha256), never .claude/ code: see _sm_sha256.
# Callers source this file by a literal relative path (no variable expansion
# on the source line), as eval.yml's trust-boundary scan requires.
#
# Evidence: every function reports `key=value` lines (one line, no newline in
# the value). When ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE is set they are appended to that file;
# else they go to the descriptor in SANDBOX_MOUNT_EVIDENCE_FD (default 1).
# resolve_arm_toggles prints JSON on stdout and no evidence.
#
# Tested by evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats (directly and through execute-agent.sh)
# and evals/tests/execute-agent.bats.
# =============================================================================

[[ "${_SANDBOX_MOUNT_LOADED:-}" == "true" ]] && return 0
_SANDBOX_MOUNT_LOADED=true

_SM_LIB_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_SM_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$_SM_LIB_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"

_sm_err() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; }

# _sm_sha256 <file>... prints "<hex>  <file>" lines, the sha256sum output shape.
# Python hashlib, not compat-lib's sha256_portable: the eval workflow runs the
# harness as the trusted copy against a PR's .claude/, so no harness script
# sources .claude/ code (eval.yml "Validate grader trust boundary"); run-arms.sh
# hashes the corpus the same way.
_sm_sha256() {
  python3 -I -c '
import hashlib, sys
for p in sys.argv[1:]:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p, "rb") as f:
        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(b)
    print(h.hexdigest() + "  " + p)' "$@"
}

# _sm_evidence <key> <value> — one key=value line to the evidence sink.
_sm_evidence() {
  local line="$1=${2//$'\n'/ }"
  if [[ -n "${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
  else
    local fd="${SANDBOX_MOUNT_EVIDENCE_FD:-1}"
    [[ "$fd" =~ ^[0-9]$ ]] || fd=1
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >&"$fd"
  fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
mount_prompt_surface() {
  local ws="$1" tree="$2" skill="${3:-}"
  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
  [[ -d "$tree/.claude" ]] || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: prompt tree has no .claude/: $tree"; return 2; }
  if [[ "$skill" == "-" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$ws/.claude"
    cp -a "$tree/.claude/." "$ws/.claude/" || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: copying .claude/ failed"; return 2; }
    printf '@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\n' > "$ws/CLAUDE.md"
    if [[ -f "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then cp "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" "$ws/.loa.config.yaml"; fi
    _sm_evidence mount "tree"
    return 0
  fi
  case "$skill" in */*|.*|'') _sm_err "invalid skill name '$skill'"; return 2 ;; esac
  local skill_src="$tree/.claude/skills/$skill"
  [[ -f "$skill_src/SKILL.md" ]] || { _sm_err "prompt tree $tree has no .claude/skills/$skill/SKILL.md"; return 2; }
  mkdir -p "$ws/.claude/skills" "$ws/.claude/loa"
  # Whole skill dir (resources included) so guarded reads inside the skill resolve.
  local skill_dst="$ws/.claude/skills/$skill"
  mkdir -p "$skill_dst"
  cp -a "$skill_src/." "$skill_dst/"
  if [[ -f "$tree/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" ]]; then
    cp "$tree/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$ws/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
  fi
  if [[ -d "$tree/.claude/rules" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$ws/.claude/rules"
    cp -a "$tree/.claude/rules/." "$ws/.claude/rules/"
  fi
  printf '@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\n' > "$ws/CLAUDE.md"
  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM+x}" && -f "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
    cp "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" "$ws/.loa.config.yaml"
  fi
  _sm_evidence mount "skill:$skill"
  return 0
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
resolve_arm_toggles() {
  local arm="$1" suite_file="${2:-}"
  [[ "$arm" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]] || { _sm_err "invalid arm id '$arm'"; return 2; }
  local found=0 entry=""
  if [[ -n "$suite_file" && -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
    # an unreadable suite file reads as "not declared" (cycle-129 behaviour: baseline still resolves to {})
    entry="$(ARM="$arm" yq -o=json -I=0 '[((.arms // [])[]), ((.ab.arms // [])[])] | map(select(.id == strenv(ARM))) | .[0] // null' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null)" \
      || entry=""
    [[ -n "$entry" && "$entry" != "null" ]] && found=1
  fi
  if [[ "$found" -eq 0 ]]; then
    [[ "$arm" == "baseline" ]] && { printf '{}'; return 0; }
    _sm_err "arm '$arm' is not declared in ${suite_file:-any suite} (arms[] / ab.arms[])"
    return 2
  fi
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.absent // false' <<<"$entry")" == "true" ]]; then
    _sm_err "arm '$arm' is declared absent in $suite_file (never run): $(jq -r '.evidence // "no evidence"' <<<"$entry")"
    return 2
  fi
  local t
  t="$(jq -c '.toggles // {}' <<<"$entry")"
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$t" || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggles are not an object in $suite_file"; return 2; }
  printf '%s' "$t"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
_sm_drop_md_section() {
  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmpdir="$3" tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp "$tmpdir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
  awk -v h="$heading" '
    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
    skip { n++; next }
    { print }
    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
  mv "$tmp" "$f"
  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
}

# Remove the first blank-line-delimited paragraph of $1 that contains one of
# the needles (tried in order, case-insensitive). Writes the removed text to
# $2; exit 1 when no needle matches.
_sm_drop_paragraph() {
  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "look for what the review did not" "Confirm the review's demotions independently" <<'PY'
import re, sys
path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
paras = re.split(r"(\n[ \t]*\n)", text)
for needle in sys.argv[3:]:
    for i in range(0, len(paras), 2):
        if needle.lower() in paras[i].lower():
            removed = paras[i]
            # drop the paragraph and the separator that follows it
            del paras[i:i + 2]
            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(paras))
            open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(removed + "\n")
            sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(1)
PY
}

# Strip every `effort:` line from the YAML frontmatter of file $1 (frontmatter
# = line 1 `---` up to the next `---`). Prints 1 when a line was removed, else 0.
_sm_strip_frontmatter_effort() {
  local f="$1" tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp "$f.XXXXXX")"
  awk '
    NR == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 1; print; next }
    fm == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 2; print; next }
    fm == 1 && /^effort:/ { n++; next }
    { print }
    END { print (n > 0 ? 1 : 0) > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
  cat "$tmp" > "$f"; rm -f "$tmp"
  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
}

# 0 when file $1's frontmatter still carries an `effort:` line.
_sm_frontmatter_has_effort() {
  awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" { exit 1 } NR > 1 && $0 == "---" { exit 1 } NR > 1 && /^effort:/ { found = 1; exit 0 } END { exit (found ? 0 : 1) }' "$1"
}

_sm_cfg_set_false() {  # _sm_cfg_set_false <cfg> <yq-path>... ; verifies each
  local cfg="$1"; shift
  [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
  local p
  for p in "$@"; do
    P="$p" yq -i 'eval(strenv(P)) = false' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    [[ "$(P="$p" yq -r 'eval(strenv(P))' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] || return 1
  done
  return 0
}

apply_arm_toggles() {
  local ws="$1" toggles="${2:-}" arm="${3:-}"
  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "apply_arm_toggles: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
  [[ -n "$toggles" ]] || toggles='{}'
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$toggles" || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggles are not a JSON object"; return 2; }
  local eval_dir="$ws/.eval"
  mkdir -p "$eval_dir"
  local key val
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
    if [[ "$key" == "effort" ]]; then
      case "$val" in low|medium|high|xhigh|max) ;; *) _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle effort=$val (want low|medium|high|xhigh|max)"; return 2 ;; esac
    elif [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
      _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)"; return 2
    fi
    case "$key" in
      companion_voice)
        _sm_cfg_set_false "$ws/.loa.config.yaml" .flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice \
          || { _sm_err "companion_voice toggle did not take effect"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
        ;;
      karpathy_block)
        local k="$ws/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md"; return 2; }
        n="$(_sm_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles' "$eval_dir")"
        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
          _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed"; return 2
        fi
        local cj="$ws/.claude/data/constraints.json" cjn="none"
        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
          # audit r1 DISS-C-008: a failed rewrite is exit 2, not a silent pass; verify afterwards
          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" \
            || { rm -f "$cj.tmp"; _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json could not be rewritten"; return 2; }
          mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
          cjn="$(jq '[(.constraints // [])[] | select(tostring | test("karpathy"; "i"))] | length' "$cj" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")"
          [[ "$cjn" == "0" ]] || { _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json still carries Karpathy rows ($cjn)"; return 2; }
        fi
        _sm_evidence karpathy_block "removed ${n} lines from CLAUDE.loa.md; constraints.json karpathy rows after: ${cjn}"
        ;;
      rule_files)
        local r gone=""
        for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
          if [[ -e "$ws/.claude/rules/$r" ]]; then rm -f "$ws/.claude/rules/$r"; gone="$gone $r"; fi
          [[ ! -e "$ws/.claude/rules/$r" ]] || { _sm_err "rule_files toggle: $r still present"; return 2; }
        done
        _sm_evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"
        ;;
      audit_delta_instruction)
        local s="$ws/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
        [[ -f "$s" ]] || { _sm_err "audit_delta_instruction toggle: no sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md"; return 2; }
        _sm_drop_paragraph "$s" "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" \
          || { _sm_err "audit_delta_instruction toggle: no delta paragraph found in the sandbox SKILL.md"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence audit_delta_instruction "removed $(wc -c < "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" | tr -d ' ') bytes (.eval/arm-removed.txt)"
        ;;
      loa_mount)
        local p left=""
        for p in .claude CLAUDE.md .loa.config.yaml; do
          if [[ -e "$ws/$p" || -L "$ws/$p" ]]; then left="$left $p"; fi
        done
        [[ -z "$left" ]] || { _sm_err "loa_mount toggle: the sandbox still holds:$left (mount_prompt_surface must be skipped)"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence loa_mount "none"
        ;;
      effort)
        local f total=0 stripped=0 still=""
        for f in "$ws"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
          [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
          total=$((total + 1))
          if [[ "$(_sm_strip_frontmatter_effort "$f")" == "1" ]]; then stripped=$((stripped + 1)); fi
          if _sm_frontmatter_has_effort "$f"; then still="$still ${f#"$ws"/}"; fi
        done
        [[ -z "$still" ]] || { _sm_err "effort toggle: effort: still in the frontmatter of:$still"; return 2; }
        local mc="$ws/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml" cat_state="absent"
        if [[ -f "$mc" ]]; then
          local nkeys
          nkeys="$(yq '[.. | select(tag == "!!map" and has("default_effort"))] | length' "$mc" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
          [[ "$nkeys" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$nkeys" -gt 0 ]] \
            || { _sm_err "effort toggle: no default_effort key in the sandbox model-config.yaml"; return 2; }
          V="$val" yq -i '(.. | select(tag == "!!map" and has("default_effort")) | .default_effort) = strenv(V)' "$mc" \
            || { _sm_err "effort toggle: yq failed on the sandbox model-config.yaml"; return 2; }
          local wrong
          wrong="$(V="$val" yq '[.. | select(tag == "!!map" and has("default_effort")) | select(.default_effort != strenv(V))] | length' "$mc" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
          [[ "$wrong" == "0" ]] || { _sm_err "effort toggle: default_effort did not take effect"; return 2; }
          cat_state="default_effort=$val in $nkeys entries"
          if [[ -f "$mc.checksum" ]]; then
            local h
            h="$(_sm_sha256 "$mc" | awk '{print $1}')"
            [[ "$h" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || { _sm_err "effort toggle: could not hash model-config.yaml"; return 2; }
            printf '%s\n' "$h" > "$mc.checksum"
            cat_state="$cat_state; .checksum refreshed"
          fi
        fi
        _sm_evidence effort "$val"
        _sm_evidence effort_skills_stripped "$stripped/$total"
        _sm_evidence effort_catalog "$cat_state"
        ;;
      gates)
        _sm_cfg_set_false "$ws/.loa.config.yaml" .flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled .flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled \
          || { _sm_err "gates toggle did not take effect"; return 2; }
        export LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false
        if [[ -n "${ARM_ENV_FILE:-}" ]]; then printf 'LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false\n' >> "$ARM_ENV_FILE"; fi
        _sm_evidence gates "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.enabled=false"
        _sm_evidence arm_env "LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false"
        ;;
      flatline)
        _sm_cfg_set_false "$ws/.loa.config.yaml" .flatline_protocol.enabled \
          || { _sm_err "flatline toggle did not take effect"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence flatline "flatline_protocol.enabled=false"
        ;;
      sprint_plan)
        _sm_evidence sprint_plan "phase set without PLAN (pipeline executor); no sprint.md materialised"
        ;;
      context_resets)
        _sm_evidence context_resets "implementer phases continue one session (pipeline executor)"
        ;;
      *) _sm_err "arm '$arm' declares unknown toggle '$key'"; return 2 ;;
    esac
  done < <(jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, (.value | tostring)] | @tsv' <<<"$toggles")
  return 0
}

regen_sandbox_manifest() {
  local ws="$1"
  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
  if [[ ! -d "$ws/.claude" ]]; then
    _sm_evidence manifest_sha256 "none"
    return 0
  fi
  local out="$ws/.claude/checksums.json" tool="${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}/tools/gen-checksums.sh" how="inline"
  if [[ -x "$tool" ]] && git -C "$ws" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 \
     && [[ -n "$(git -C "$ws" ls-files .claude 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ]]; then
    "$tool" --root "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: $tool --root $ws failed"; return 2; }
    how="gen-checksums.sh"
  else
    local list="$ws/.eval/.manifest-files" sums="$ws/.eval/.manifest-sums"
    mkdir -p "$ws/.eval"
    ( cd "$ws" && find .claude -type f ! -path '.claude/overrides/*' ! -path '.claude/checksums.json' -print ) \
      | LC_ALL=C sort > "$list"
    if grep -q '\\' "$list"; then _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: a path under .claude/ holds a backslash"; rm -f "$list"; return 2; fi
    : > "$sums"
    local -a batch=()
    local f
    while IFS= read -r f; do
      batch+=("$f")
      if [[ ${#batch[@]} -ge 200 ]]; then
        ( cd "$ws" && _sm_sha256 "${batch[@]}" ) >> "$sums" || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: hashing failed"; return 2; }
        batch=()
      fi
    done < "$list"
    if [[ ${#batch[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
      ( cd "$ws" && _sm_sha256 "${batch[@]}" ) >> "$sums" || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: hashing failed"; return 2; }
    fi
    jq -Rn --arg generated "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '
      {generated: $generated, algorithm: "sha256",
       files: ([inputs | select(length > 0) | capture("^(?<h>[0-9a-f]{64})  (?<p>.+)$") | {key: .p, value: .h}] | from_entries)}' \
      < "$sums" > "$out.tmp" || { rm -f "$out.tmp" "$list" "$sums"; _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: could not write the manifest"; return 2; }
    mv "$out.tmp" "$out"
    rm -f "$list" "$sums"
  fi
  jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$out" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: $out is not a manifest"; return 2; }
  local digest
  digest="$(_sm_sha256 "$out" | awk '{print $1}')"
  _sm_evidence manifest_files "$(jq '.files | length' "$out") ($how)"
  _sm_evidence manifest_sha256 "$digest"
  return 0
}

  return 0

+# --- cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.6 (PRD AC-3.1, AC-3.2, AC-5.6; sprint AC-1.6, AC-1.10;
+# DEC-0421, DEC-0431, DEC-0433). The ablation-2.0 arms through execute-agent.sh, and
+# lib/sandbox-mount.sh called directly for the pipeline-shaped (whole-tree) mount.
+
+ABL_SUITE_REL="evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml"
+LIB_REL="evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh"
+
+lib() {  # lib <function> <args…> — one library call in a strict subshell
+  bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; source "$1"; shift; "$@"' _ "$REPO_ROOT/$LIB_REL" "$@"
+}
+
+# The prompt tree as the pipeline mounts it: a catalog with two default_effort
+# entries and its .checksum, a second skill with an effort line, the beads
+# state script, and an overrides/ file the manifest must skip.
+extend_tree() {
+  mkdir -p "$PT/.claude/defaults" "$PT/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks" "$PT/.claude/scripts/beads" "$PT/.claude/overrides"
+  printf '%s\n' "providers:" "  anthropic:" "    models:" "      claude-opus-5-5:" "        params:" "          default_effort: high" \
+    "      claude-fable-5-1:" "        params:" "          default_effort: xhigh" > "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml"
+  sha256sum_of "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml" > "$PT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml.checksum"
+  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: implementing-tasks" "effort: xhigh" "model: opus" "---" "# Implement" "effort: this body line stays" \
+    > "$PT/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md"
+  cp "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh" "$PT/.claude/scripts/beads/"
+  echo "operator override" > "$PT/.claude/overrides/local.md"
+}
+sha256sum_of() { bash -c 'source "$1"; sha256_portable "$2" | cut -d" " -f1' _ "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh" "$1"; }
+
+# check-loa.sh's own integrity check, run inside the sandbox (its cwd-relative manifest)
+integrity_in() {
+  ( cd "$1" && bash -c 'source "$1" && { check_integrity || true; } && echo "FAILURES=$FAILURES"' _ "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh" )
+}

content.text:
I found 7 issues worth reporting, plus 2 low-confidence notes. The checksum is fine: `.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml.checksum` (`ba767f53…122c`) matches the sha256 of the head `model-config.yaml`, and it uses the bare-hex format of the base file.

## Findings

**1. CI path filters never trigger the new gates** (`.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:21-45` push, `:47-71` pull_request), high confidence.
The new steps at :175-178 (`check-manifest-paths.sh`, `gen-checksums.sh --check`) and :212-224 (`evals/tests`) only run if the workflow fires. The trigger lists leave out:
- `tools/gen-checksums.sh`, `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh` and `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh`
- `evals/**`
- most of the tracked `.claude/` tree (`skills/**` except two, `loa/**`, `rules/**`, `data/**`, `protocols/**`)

So a PR that edits only `evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh` never runs the eval-harness bats. A PR that edits `.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md` without regenerating the manifest passes. The drift then fails some later, unrelated PR that does touch `.claude/scripts/**`.

**2. Committed manifest looks stale**, medium confidence.
`tests/unit/check-manifest-paths.bats:88-92` (MP-6) says the repo commits `.claude/checksums.json`. This PR changes three tracked `.claude/` files (`check-loa.sh`, `preflight.sh`, `model-config.yaml`) plus `model-config.yaml.checksum`, but `checksums.json` is not in the diff. If it is committed, `gen-checksums.sh --check` (`bats-tests.yml:178`) reports those entries as `changed` and exits 1. Medium only because the snapshot may be scoped down to 72 files.

**3. Non-ASCII paths are wrongly flagged as untracked** (`tools/check-manifest-paths.sh:80`), high confidence.
`git ls-files -- .claude` runs without `-z` or `-c core.quotePath=false`, so git prints `".claude/caf\303\251.md"`. `gen-checksums.sh:102` uses `-z` and stores the raw UTF-8 path. I reproduced it: `gen-checksums.sh --check` says OK, while `check-manifest-paths.sh` reports `untracked (other=1)` and exits 1. Paths containing `"` hit the same problem.

**4. Errors are ignored inside `run_step`** (`tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:103-109`, used at :137, :150, :156), high confidence.
`if ! "$@"` turns off `set -e` for the whole function body, so only the last command's status counts. In `overlay` (:122-136), a failed `mkdir`, `rm` or `cp`, or a failed `git add -A`, is ignored. Then `git commit --allow-empty` succeeds anyway. The proof then runs against REF without the work-tree state, instead of exiting 3 as documented (:46-47). `init_downstream` and `do_mount` are affected the same way.

**5. Harness runs the PR's own code** (`evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:383-387`), medium confidence.
`regen_sandbox_manifest` runs `${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE}/tools/gen-checksums.sh`, which sources `$EVAL_PROMPT_TREE/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh`. That is the PR-controlled tree. The file's own header (:96-100) says hashing uses Python precisely so no harness script runs `.claude/` code. `init_sandbox_beads` (:511-513) also runs the sandbox's `.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh`. In `pipeline-run.sh` the first path is hard to reach, because `.claude` is excluded from the sandbox git repo. In `execute-agent.sh` the workspace comes from the caller, so a git workspace that tracks `.claude` reaches it.

**6. Preflight count can disagree in standard-mode downstreams** (`.claude/scripts/preflight.sh:189-197`), medium-low confidence.
The comment says the manifest comes from the tracked tree via `gen-checksums.sh`. But `gen-checksums.sh:6-10` says `mount-loa.sh` and `update.sh` still build it with `find`. A downstream that commits `.claude/` now gets a git-tracked count compared against a `find`-based manifest count. Any untracked or ignored file under `.claude/` then gives a false count-mismatch warning that the old find-vs-find comparison did not. It is only a warning.

**7. Test header refers to a test that doesn't exist** (`tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats:8-9`), high confidence, trivial.
It says "the live manifest is only read by GC-8", but the file stops at GC-7. Nothing in this file checks the live manifest.

**8. Symlinks are copied as symlinks** (`evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:131, 144, 150`), low confidence.
`cp -a` keeps symlinks in the prompt tree as links. The contract (:18-19) says files are copied, never a symlink to the tree. An absolute symlink in a PR's `.claude/` would point the sandbox agent outside the sandbox. The inline manifest (`find -type f`, :391) also leaves these entries out, so they are not covered by integrity evidence.

**9. Two smaller items**, low confidence.
- `sandbox-mount.sh:198`: `mv` of a `mktemp` file makes `CLAUDE.loa.md` mode 0600. `_sm_strip_frontmatter_effort` keeps permissions by using `cat >`.
- `sandbox-mount.sh:286`: carried over unchanged from `execute-agent.sh`. `(.constraints // []) |= …` fails in jq 1.6 ("Invalid path expression with result []") when `constraints.json` has no `.constraints` key, so the karpathy toggle exits 2 even though there is nothing to remove.

## Checked and fine
- `check-loa.sh`: the TSV read loop, the not-mounted branch (`.loa/${file}`), and the added `return 0`. The `return 0` actually fixes an old `set -e` early exit when drift was found.
- `resolve_arm_toggles` (ran with yq 4.40: undeclared, absent and baseline arms behave as documented) and the frontmatter effort strip/detect pair.
- The `--check` diff logic and exit codes in `gen-checksums.sh`, and the class order in `check-manifest-paths.sh`, which matches MP-4.

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.1)
#
# execute-agent.sh applies a control arm's toggles to the sandbox copy only.
# Every assertion here reads the sandbox as the EXECUTOR saw it: the CLI stub
# snapshots CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .loa.config.yaml and the appended system
# prompt at the moment it starts (STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR), after every
# materialisation step. The arm ids and toggles come from the real suite
# files; the prompt tree is a synthetic fixture so later prose edits to the
# live kernel cannot change what this test proves.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  EXEC="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh"
  REVIEW_SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/review-recall.yaml"
  AUDIT_SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/audit-recall.yaml"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/at.XXXXXX")"
  WS="$T/ws"; SNAP="$T/snap"
  mkdir -p "$WS"
  ( cd "$WS" && git init -q && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q --allow-empty -m init )
  export EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub.sh"
  export EVAL_MODEL="claude-fable-5-1"
  export STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR="$SNAP"
  unset LOA_EVAL_ARM LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT EVAL_EFFORT

  # --- synthetic prompt tree (the shape of 864069f2) ---
  PT="$T/tree"
  mkdir -p "$PT/.claude/loa" "$PT/.claude/rules" "$PT/.claude/data" \
    "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code" "$PT/.claude/skills/auditing-security"
  printf '%s\n' "# Loa Framework Instructions" "" "## Three-Zone Model" "" "zones" "" \
    "## Karpathy Principles" "" "Every code-touching turn." "" "1. **Think before coding** — state assumptions." "" \
    "## Process Compliance" "" "rules" > "$PT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
  echo "# Git Stash Safety" > "$PT/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md"
  echo "# Skill Frontmatter Invariants" > "$PT/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md"
  printf '%s\n' "---" "paths:" '  - "grimoires/**"' "---" "# zone state" > "$PT/.claude/rules/zone-state.md"
  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: reviewing-code" "---" "# Review" "Review the diff." > "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: auditing-security" "---" "# Audit" "" "### Coverage" "" \
    "Report every finding you actually observe." "" \
    "Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under" \
    "\`excluded\`, either confirm it or tally it as a finding of your own." "" \
    "## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally" "" "Count every finding." > "$PT/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
  printf '%s\n' "flatline_protocol:" "  code_review:" "    enabled: true" "  security_audit:" "    enabled: true" > "$PT/.loa.config.yaml"
  ( cd "$PT" && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m tree )
  export EVAL_PROMPT_TREE="$PT"

  for s in reviewing-code auditing-security; do
    cat > "$T/task-$s.yaml" <<YAML
id: at-$s
schema_version: 1
skill: $s
category: skill-quality
fixture: hello-world-ts
description: "arm toggle task"
prompt: "Read the instructions and carry them out."
agent:
  skill: $s
  artifacts: [review.md]
graders:
  - type: code
    script: file-exists.sh
    args: ["review.md"]
YAML
  done
}

teardown() {
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

run_arm() {  # run_arm <arm> <suite-file> <skill>
  LOA_EVAL_ARM="$1" LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE="$2" run "$EXEC" --task-yaml "$T/task-$3.yaml" --workspace "$WS"

#

# run-ablation.sh would shape them (SDD §3.4, §3.6).

# Usage: evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/regen.sh
# Consumers: evals/tests/ablation-row.bats, evals/tests/took-effect.bats
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
FIX="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
GEN="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/abl-fixture.XXXXXX")"
trap 'chmod -R u+rwx "$GEN" 2>/dev/null; find "$GEN" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null; rmdir "$GEN" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT

mkdir -p "$H/lib"
cp "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh" "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/fingerprint.sh" "$H/"
cp -a "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/lib/phase-prompts" "$H/lib/"
cp "$FIX/mount-lib-stub.sh" "$H/lib/sandbox-mount.sh"
PR="$H/pipeline-run.sh"

# Copy of evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml as implementer B landed it (Sprint 258); the fixture runs and
# evals/tests/{pipeline-run,ablation-row,took-effect}.bats read this copy so the tests do not move with the live suite.
# =============================================================================
# evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml — cycle-130 Loa 2.0 component ablation suite
#
# SDD §3.3 (structure reproduced), extended by Sprint 258 Task 1.6: the
# tasks block with the smoke root, phase_defaults, phase_sets, cost_hint, each
# arm's phase-set override and took-effect rule ids, and the full pre-registered
# rules block (D-A5; mirrored in NOTES before the first run, DEC-0383).
#
# Readers: execute-agent.sh / lib/sandbox-mount.sh (arms[].toggles via
# resolve_arm_toggles), pipeline-run.sh (phase_defaults, phase_sets,
# arms[].phases, arms[].effort), took-effect.sh (arms[].took_effect),
# run-ablation.sh (trials, caps, priority, cut_ladder, arms[].task_types),
# ablation-report.py (rules), validate-suite.sh (arm ids for the leakage check,
# task_types against the known types).
#
# task_types: `all` | `build` (= feature-build, bug-fix, refactor) |
#   `review-catch` | a single build type. An arm is never scheduled, and a row
#   never reported, on a type outside its declaration (DEC-0400, DEC-0406).
# took_effect: rule ids took-effect.sh evaluates per trial (DEC-0418); a miss is
#   infrastructure_error and pauses the arm. `applicability_refused` is the
#   smoke's evidence line that the planner refused the arm on a review-catch task.
# =============================================================================
name: ablation-2.0
version: 1
source_commit: "<sprint-258-commit>"   # the lead sets the Sprint 258 commit (rc.5 plus the mount fix; F2, DEC-0392)
agy_opt_in: false
tasks:
  root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks
  manifest: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/MANIFEST.sha256
  smoke_root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke
suite_version: 1
trials: {build: 3, review-catch: 3}      # D-A4: review-catch trials 3, not 5, under the gate pipeline
cut_ladder: ["A5, A6, A7 not run", "A2 and A3 build trials 3 -> 2", "A3 review-catch trials 3 -> 2"]   # DEC-0397; A0, A1, A4 keep 3
caps: {cycle_usd: 1500, run_usd: 12, reserve_usd: 250}   # reserve released to A7 when the re-verification rule needs no run (DEC-0398)
priority: [a0_bare, a1_full, a2_no_sprint_plan, a3_one_voice, a4_no_gates, a7_effort_medium, a5_no_flatline, a6_one_window]
cost_hint: {build: 7, review-catch: 8}   # USD per run before any actual exists (run-arms/run-ablation est_next fallback)

# Session defaults per phase (SDD D-4.3). A6's continued session carries the
# caps of the phase it is in; A0's BARE caps are PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX.
phase_defaults:
  models:
    PLAN: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    IMPLEMENT: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    FIX: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    BARE: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    REVIEW: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
    AUDIT: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
  max_turns: {PLAN: 30, IMPLEMENT: 60, REVIEW: 40, FIX: 40, AUDIT: 40, BARE: 170}
  timeout_min: {PLAN: 15, IMPLEMENT: 25, REVIEW: 20, FIX: 15, AUDIT: 20, BARE: 70}

rules:   # D-A5: pre-registered, mirrored in NOTES
  threshold_points: 0.03
  cost_lower_pct: 15
  bootstrap: {resamples: 10000, level: 0.90, paired: true, units: {hidden_test_pass_rate: tasks, defect_catch_rate: defects}, also_report: {defect_catch_rate: tasks}}   # DEC-0399
  primaries_by_arm: {build_only: [hidden_test_pass_rate], all_types: [hidden_test_pass_rate, defect_catch_rate]}   # DEC-0400
  cap_failure: counts_as_failed            # 0 on each applicable primary (DEC-0393)
  exclusion: {statuses: [degraded, contaminated, interrupted], mode: pairwise, inconclusive_above_share: 0.25}
  sensitivity_figure: cap_failures_excluded  # printed, never decides
  multiple_comparisons: none                 # expected false positives at 0.90 over 6 components printed
  drift_guard: {cli_version: fixed_per_batch, model_ids: fixed_per_batch}   # DEC-0407
  order: trial_major_seeded_shuffle_within_block
  took_effect_per_trial: true                # a miss → infrastructure_error, arm paused until --clear-arm (DEC-0418)
  predicates:                                # DEC-0416; d = arm − A1 point estimate, [lo, hi] its 90 % interval, c/w = cost/wall-clock Δ %
    investigate: "any applicable primary has lo > 0"
    keep: "else any applicable primary has d < -0.03 and hi < 0"
    inconclusive: "else any applicable primary has d < -0.03, or the arm's excluded share > 0.25, or no valid pair"
    remove: "else every applicable primary has d >= -0.03 and (c <= -15 or w <= -15)"
    simplify: "else (every applicable primary within -0.03, cost similar)"

  mde_cut: 0.10   # sprint Task 3.4: an arm whose MDE at affordable trials exceeds this is pre-declared inconclusive_by_power and not run

STARTED="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
STATE="running"
# per-arm counters (indexed arrays parallel to ARMS — bash 3.2 has no maps)
DONE=() FAILED=() PLANNED=()
for i in "${!ARMS[@]}"; do DONE[$i]=0; FAILED[$i]=0; PLANNED[$i]=$(( ${#FIXTURES[@]} * TRIALS )); done
# spend accounting (--max-usd): batch spend, per-arm and pooled completed-cost sums
SPENT=0 CUT_JSON=null POOL_SUM=0 POOL_N=0
ARM_SUM=() ARM_N=()
for i in "${!ARMS[@]}"; do ARM_SUM[$i]=0; ARM_N[$i]=0; done
fadd() { awk -v a="$1" -v b="$2" 'BEGIN { printf "%.10g", a + b }'; }
arm_index() { local i; for i in "${!ARMS[@]}"; do [[ "${ARMS[$i]}" == "$1" ]] && { echo "$i"; return; }; done; echo -1; }

write_status() {
  local per='{}' i finished=null
  for i in "${!ARMS[@]}"; do
    per="$(jq -c --arg a "${ARMS[$i]}" --argjson d "${DONE[$i]}" --argjson f "${FAILED[$i]}" --argjson p "${PLANNED[$i]}" \
      '. + {($a): {trials_done: $d, trials_failed: $f, trials_planned: $p}}' <<<"$per")"
  done
  [[ "$STATE" != "running" ]] && finished="\"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\""
  jq -n --arg state "$STATE" --argjson per "$per" --arg src "$SRC_FULL" --arg model "$MODEL" \
    --arg started "$STARTED" --argjson finished "$finished" --arg batch "$BATCH" --arg suite "$SUITE" \
    --argjson cut "$CUT_JSON" --argjson screen "$SCREEN" --arg spent "$SPENT" --arg max_usd "$MAX_USD" \
    '{schema_version: 1, suite: $suite, batch: $batch, state: $state, per_arm: $per,
      source_commit: $src, model_id: $model, started: $started, finished: $finished}
     + (if $max_usd == "" then {} else {spend: {spent_usd: ($spent | tonumber), max_usd: ($max_usd | tonumber)}} end)
     + (if $cut == null then {} else {cut_reason: $cut.reason, cut: $cut} end)
     + (if $screen then {screen: true} else {} end)' > "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json.tmp"
  mv "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json.tmp" "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json"
  # a screening batch never touches the suite-level aggregate (bd-j4lwr)
  [[ "$SCREEN" == "true" ]] || aggregate_status
}

# The suite-level STATUS.json merges every batch: counters add per arm; the
# state is failed > running > partial > complete; source/model must agree.
aggregate_status() {
  local agg="$SUITE_DIR/STATUS.json" lockd="$SUITE_DIR/.status.lock" n=0
  until mkdir "$lockd" 2>/dev/null; do n=$((n + 1)); [[ $n -gt 50 ]] && return 0; sleep 0.1; done
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  jq -s --arg suite "$SUITE" '
    def rank: {"failed": 4, "running": 3, "partial": 2, "complete": 1}[.] // 4;
    (map(.state) | max_by(rank)) as $state |
    {schema_version: 1, suite: $suite, state: $state,
     batches: map({batch, state, started, finished}),
     cuts: [.[] | select(.cut != null) | .cut + {batch}],
     per_arm: (reduce (.[] | .per_arm | to_entries[]) as $e ({};
        .[$e.key] |= {trials_done: ((.trials_done // 0) + $e.value.trials_done),
                      trials_failed: ((.trials_failed // 0) + $e.value.trials_failed),
                      trials_planned: ((.trials_planned // 0) + $e.value.trials_planned)})),
     source_commit: (map(.source_commit) | unique | if length == 1 then .[0] else "MIXED" end),
     model_id: (map(.model_id) | unique | if length == 1 then .[0] else "MIXED" end),
     started: (map(.started) | min), finished: (if $state == "running" then null else (map(.finished) | max) end)}' \
    $(find "$SUITE_DIR" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name STATUS.json ! -path "$SUITE_DIR/screen-*" | sort) > "$agg.tmp" 2>/dev/null \
    && mv "$agg.tmp" "$agg"
  rmdir "$lockd" 2>/dev/null || true
}
set_state() { STATE="$1"; write_status; }
  [[ "$f" =~ ^pr-[0-9]{2}$ ]] || die "invalid fixture id '$f' (want pr-NN)"
  [[ -d "$CORPUS_DIR/$f" ]] || die "fixture not found: $CORPUS_DIR/$f"
  [[ -f "$CORPUS_DIR/manifests/$f.json" ]] || die "hidden manifest not found for $f"
  [[ -f "$EVALS_DIR/tasks/$SUITE/$TASK_PREFIX-$f.yaml" ]] || die "task not found: tasks/$SUITE/$TASK_PREFIX-$f.yaml"
  if [[ "$(jq -r 'if has("approved") then .approved else true end' "$CORPUS_DIR/manifests/$f.json")" != "true" \
        && "$ALLOW_UNAPPROVED" != "true" ]]; then
    die "$f: labels.tsv is not approved yet (seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve $f --by '<who> <date>'), or pass --allow-unapproved"
  fi
done

I found 7 defects in scope. The most important are the test assertions that can't fail; none of the harness bugs breaks the main code paths. The fixture run directories (`evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`) aren't in the snapshot, so I couldn't run took-effect.bats or ablation-row.bats. I couldn't run validate-suite.bats or freeze.bats either, because the smoke tasks, `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh` and `review-recall.yaml` are missing. Of the files in scope, only spend.bats passes as-is; I checked the rest by reading the code and with small reproductions (bats, jq and bash snippets under `$HOME`, since `/tmp` is noexec).

### Findings (paths relative to `/workspace/pr/head`)

**1. Status assertions that can never fail.** `evals/tests/took-effect.bats:147`, `evals/tests/ablation-row.bats:112, 115, 118, 140`. High confidence.
- These lines use the form `[ "$status" -eq 1 ] && [[ ... ]]` (or `&& line ... | grep -q`), and none of them is the last command in its test.
- When `[ "$status" -eq 1 ]` is false, the `&&` list fails on a non-final command, so neither errexit nor bats' ERR trap fires and the test carries on.
- I confirmed this with a small bats file: it passes with `status=0`.
- The effect: a regression where `--validate` accepts a bad status, a bad task_type, degraded-without-reason, or an ungraded build row (line 140) would pass. The same goes for the gate-shares-REVIEW-session case in took-effect.
- `ablation-row.bats:195` and `took-effect.bats:151` are safe only because each is the last line of its test. Line 99 is fine because of its `|| { ...; return 1; }`.

**2. took-effect.sh passes several rules on a corrupt `meta/pipeline.json`.** `evals/harness/took-effect.sh:128-131, 139-140, 157-158, 273-277`. Medium confidence.
- Line 311 only checks that the file exists. Each rule runs inside `if`, which turns errexit off, so a failing jq just leaves an empty string.
- `[[ "" -eq 0 ]]` is true, so `no_plan_phase` and `no_gate_phases` report OK.
- In `all_phases_present`, both `want` (the `--argjson tg` call fails) and `got` come out empty, so it reports `OK phases `.
- `applicability_refused` reports "applicable:  in task_types" for an empty type.
- I reproduced this. Each arm's overall verdict is still FAIL only because `integrity_clean` fails independently, so per-rule evidence is unreliable and the overall result relies on that one rule.

**3. Doc says three stopped-early statuses; code accepts a fourth.** `evals/harness/took-effect.sh:133`. Low–medium confidence.
- The header (lines 16-19) says a prefix of the phase set passes only for `cap_failure|agent_error|interrupted`.
- The code also accepts `running`, so a run whose driver died mid-way passes `all_phases_present` on any prefix.

**4. Under `--max-usd`, a transport-retry's first attempt is dropped from spend.** `evals/harness/run-arms.sh:454` and `:506`. Medium confidence.
- On a transport failure (rate limit, overloaded, session limit, timeout), `executor` is reset to `null` before the retry.
- Only the final attempt's `executor.total_cost_usd` reaches the row, which `collect` adds to `SPENT`.
- Whatever attempt 1 cost (it may have done real work before a session or usage limit hit) never enters `SPENT`, so the cap can be overshot.

**5. `--max-usd` "positive" check is a string compare.** `evals/harness/run-arms.sh:121`. Low–medium confidence.
- `[[ "$MAX_USD" != "0" ]]` is a string comparison, so `0.0`, `00` and `0.00` pass `usd_ok` and are accepted.
- The batch is then cut at trial 1 (`0 + est > 0`) and exits 1 (partial) instead of exiting 2 as documented ("must be a positive amount"). RA-10 only tests the literal `0`.

**6. Copy failures during mounting are no longer fatal (regression in `execute-agent.sh`).** `evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:207`, together with `lib/sandbox-mount.sh:144-152`. Medium confidence.
- In base, `cp -a "$skill_src/." ...`, the `CLAUDE.loa.md` copy and the `rules/` copy ran at top level under `set -e`, so any failure aborted the run.
- They now run inside `mount_prompt_surface ... || exit 2`. Being called from an `||` list turns off errexit for the whole function body.
- Those `cp` calls have no `|| return 2` of their own, so a failed copy is ignored, the function returns 0, and the executor starts with an incomplete sandbox.

**7. A missing option value exits 1 silently instead of 2.** `evals/harness/spend.sh:49, 55, 56`. Low confidence.
- `--since`, `--cap` or `--reserve` given as the last argument makes `shift 2` fail with fewer than 2 arguments; `set -e` then exits with status 1 and no message.
- The documented contract is exit 2 for usage errors, and 1 means an unreadable file. I reproduced this with `spend.sh ... --since` (rc=1, no output).
- The same `"${2:-}"; shift 2` pattern appears in `validate-suite.sh:62,65`, `freeze.sh:43`, `took-effect.sh:69-72` and `ablation-row.sh:73-81`.

### Minor test gaps (low confidence)
- **`evals/tests/took-effect.bats:61-66`:** the title says "OK on A0; FAIL when audit.jsonl exists", but the OK case is never asserted; the file is created before the first run.
- **`evals/tests/spend.bats:83-88`:** the title says the default cap and reserve come from the suite file, but the test asserts only `reserve_usd`. `cap_usd` is read first from `.loa.config.yaml` (`spend.sh:75`), so a repo config value would go unnoticed.

### Checked and found correct
- **spend.sh:** the arithmetic (micro-dollars ÷ 1e6, run_id dedup, headroom sign) and every expected value in spend.bats.
- **run-arms.sh:** the `budget_gate` reserve/cut arithmetic against the walkthroughs in RA-6 and RA-9, and the `reap(inflight)` wait. `reap 0` would loop forever, but it can't be reached.
- **run-arms.sh:** the `cost_hint` map lookup with yq, `aggregate_status`'s `cuts` and screen-batch exclusion, and the screen-table jq.
- **ablation-row.sh:** the `--validate` jq logic, which I exercised.
- **freeze.sh, fingerprint.sh, `ablation-2.0.yaml`:** the freeze/check diff, the fingerprint hashing, and the cap numbers (BARE caps 170/70 = PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2×FIX).

# _sm_sha256 <file>... prints "<hex>  <file>" lines, the sha256sum output shape.

_sm_sha256() {

import hashlib, sys
for p in sys.argv[1:]:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p, "rb") as f:

}

content.text:
I found 9 defects across `pipeline-run.sh`, `Dockerfile.ablation` and `pipeline-run.bats`; the two most serious are a container escape through git and secret leakage through symlinks. Paths are relative to `/workspace/pr/head`.

I ran the bats suite on a copy under `/workspace/.eval/tmp/prc`, because the frozen files have no exec bits and `/tmp` is mounted noexec. The local jq is 1.6, which breaks the driver (finding 3), so I edited the copy to get past that. Only 4 tests still fail after that (env capture, A6, A0, A7), and I didn't trace them (finding 3 is the likely cause). Findings 1 and 9 are confirmed by running them; the rest come from reading the code.

### pipeline-run.sh

1. **Lines 446–448, 783–787: the agent can run code on the host through git (high).** After IMPLEMENT/FIX, the driver runs `git add`, `commit` and `bundle` on the host, against the sandbox's `.git`. In container mode `/workspace` (including `.git`) is writable by the agent. `sgit` only neutralises the global and system git config. The repo's own `.git/config` (`core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`) and `.git/hooks/*` stay under agent control. I confirmed that `core.fsmonitor` set in the repo config runs a command under exactly `sgit`'s env when `git add -A` runs. This undoes the container isolation (DEC-0411): host code runs as the operator, who can read `~/.claude/.credentials.json` and `~/.aws`.

2. **Lines 773–778: host files can be copied into `eval/` through symlinks (medium-high).** `cp` follows symlinks, and `[[ -f ]]` checks the link target on the host. A container agent can make `adversarial-*.json`, `.eval/model-invoke.jsonl` or `.eval/cost-ledger.jsonl` symlinks to absolute host paths such as `~/.aws/credentials`. The driver then copies those files into `eval/`, which is outside `meta/` and so is not covered by the "grader never reads meta/" rule. The ledger is also parsed from that file at lines 769–771.

3. **Lines 702/708, 816/826, 881–882: the driver doesn't work with jq 1.6 (medium; confirmed with jq 1.6).** `$label` is a syntax error in jq 1.6 ("unexpected label"), so every run fails as `infrastructure_error`. Separately, `printf '%s\0' … | jq -Rs 'split("\u0000") | .[:-1]'` (lines 704–707) loses the last argv/env element on 1.6. Debian bookworm (the image base) and Ubuntu 22.04 ship jq 1.6, and no minimum version is checked or documented. CI on ubuntu-latest (jq 1.7.1) hides this.

4. **Lines 857–862: launcher failures are counted as agent errors (medium-high).** Exit 125 (docker daemon error, container-name conflict, image vanished), 126 and 127 (`claude`/`python3`/`timeout` not found) all become `agent_error`, exit 1. The header (line 99) says CLI/docker/image missing is infrastructure, exit 2. These count against the arm as model failures. Also, `python3` (needed for the env shim) is not in the tool check at line 167.

5. **Lines 644–741: an interrupt just before launch is missed (medium).** If SIGTERM/INT arrives after the line-899 check but before `CUR_PID=$!` (during `build_prompt`, `leak_scan`, `price_for`), `kill_phase` has nothing to kill. The phase still launches, the watchdog loop breaks on `INTERRUPTED`, and the `wait` at line 741 blocks for the whole phase (up to its timeout) while it keeps spending. Nothing re-kills the child after the break.

6. **Lines 577–596, 718: the price cache never works (high confidence, low impact).** `prices="$(price_for …)"` runs in a subshell, so the `PRICE_CACHE` update is lost and `pricing.py` runs every phase. This contradicts "fetched once per model" (line 91).

7. **Doc/code mismatches (high confidence, low impact).**
   - Line 50 documents `index.json` keys as `IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2`; line 788 writes lowercase `implement|fix1|fix2` plus `base`.
   - Line 85 says the image has codex 0.137.0; `Dockerfile.ablation` line 25 pins 0.162.1.

### evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation

8. **Lines 19–20: dead build stage (low-medium).** The `brbuild` stage is never copied from, and the file's own comment says beads_rust 0.2.6 "is not on crates.io". With the legacy builder (no BuildKit) the build fails there. The `rust:1-bookworm` base is also unpinned, unlike the other base image.

### evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats

9. **Many assertions never fail (high; confirmed with bats 1.13).** Bash's `set -e`/ERR trap ignores a `! cmd` that isn't the test's last command, and any non-final command in an `&&` list. I checked both cases with a two-test bats file; both pass.
   - **No-op negations:**
     - Line 237: `PATH=/evil` never reaching the CLI is unverified, though the test title claims "LOA_* keys only".
     - Line 332: "no effort: line left" is unverified.
     - Line 339: "no --effort flag" is unverified.
     - Lines 391, 392: no "hidden" or defect key in prompts is unverified.
     - Line 394: in the loop, only the last arm id is effectively checked.
     - Line 610: the meta-boundary test's core assertion, that no arm id appears in `sandbox/`, `snapshots/`, `transcripts/` or `eval/`, is unverified.
     - Lines 652, 668, 669: credential and secret absence in the docker argv and env is unverified.
     - Line 726: the token not being in the stub logs is unverified.
   - **`&&` lists where only the last check counts:** lines 201, 202, 204, 209 (`.claude/` absent from the snapshot is unchecked), 294, 311, 390, 504 and 548.
   - **Tautology:** line 157 checks nothing about the script.

    The fix is to write these as `run ! …` or `! cmd || false`, and split the `&&` lists into separate lines.

Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
The verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: 21 findings, one per line in the `head/<path>:<line> — …` format, ending with the verdict line. I confirmed most of them against the code myself. Three parallel reviewers covered the harness; I checked their findings before including them.

**Blocking:**
- **The agent can run commands on the host (`pipeline-run.sh:446`).** After the IMPLEMENT and FIX phases, the driver runs `git add`, `commit` and `bundle` on the host against the sandbox's `.git`. In container mode that directory is writable by the agent, so a repo-local `core.fsmonitor`, hooks path or hook script runs as the operator. That defeats the container isolation.
- **Host files can leak through symlinks (`pipeline-run.sh:775`).** The driver copies the sandbox's ledger, model-invoke log and `adversarial-*.json` files with `cp`, which follows symlinks. An agent-planted link can pull files like `~/.aws/credentials` into `eval/`, which the graders read.
- **Trust boundary broken (`sandbox-mount.sh:383`).** `regen_sandbox_manifest` runs the PR tree's `gen-checksums.sh`, which sources the PR's own `.claude/` code. The library's header says it hashes with Python precisely to avoid that.
- **Copy failures are no longer fatal (`execute-agent.sh:207`).** The skill and rules copies now run inside `mount_prompt_surface … || exit 2`, which turns off `set -e`. A failed copy goes unnoticed and the agent runs on an incomplete sandbox.
- **Many test assertions can't fail.** `! cmd` and `[ … ] && [[ … ]]` lines that aren't the last line of a test are never enforced. This covers the secret-leak and arm-id-leak checks in `pipeline-run.bats`, the `--validate` rejections in `ablation-row.bats`, and a session-sharing case in `took-effect.bats`.
- **CI won't run, or will fail.** The new gates were added without widening the workflow's path filters, so PRs that only touch `evals/**` or the new `tools/` scripts never run them. Separately, this PR edits tracked `.claude/` files without regenerating `.claude/checksums.json`, so the new `gen-checksums.sh --check` gate should fail on this PR itself. That one is less certain, because the committed manifest isn't in the frozen snapshot.

**Smaller issues:**
- The run-level `--max-usd` cap doesn't count the cost of a retried first attempt, and it accepts `0.0`.
- `took-effect.sh` reports several rules as OK when `meta/pipeline.json` is corrupt, and it accepts a `running` status that its header doesn't list.
- `fresh-mount-proof.sh` ignores failed steps inside `run_step`.
- `check-manifest-paths.sh` flags non-ASCII paths as untracked because it doesn't use `-z`.
- Launcher failures (exit 125–127) are scored as agent errors instead of infrastructure errors.
- The price cache never persists, `pipeline-run.sh` breaks on jq 1.6, the snapshot index keys don't match the header, and missing option values in `spend.sh` exit 1 instead of 2.

The framework-side changes look fine. The model-config checksum matches its file, and `check-loa.sh`'s new `return 0` actually fixes an old early exit when drift was found.

About half the new bats files couldn't run here, because the snapshot is missing fixture run directories and parts of `.claude/`. `spend.bats` passes. One reviewer ran `pipeline-run.bats` on a copy patched past the jq 1.6 problem; four tests still failed and weren't traced, though the jq incompatibility is the likely cause. The rest of the findings come from reading the code plus small reproductions.

- **Trust boundary broken (`sandbox-mount.sh:383`).** `regen_sandbox_manifest` runs the PR tree's `gen-checksums.sh`, which sources the PR's own `.claude/` code. The library's header says it hashes with Python precisely to avoid that.
- **Copy failures are no longer fatal (`execute-agent.sh:207`).** The skill and rules copies now run inside `mount_prompt_surface … || exit 2`, which turns off `set -e`. A failed copy goes unnoticed and the agent runs on an incomplete sandbox.
- **Many test assertions can't fail.** `! cmd` and `[ … ] && [[ … ]]` lines that aren't the last line of a test are never enforced. This covers the secret-leak and arm-id-leak checks in `pipeline-run.bats`, the `--validate` rejections in `ablation-row.bats`, and a session-sharing case in `took-effect.bats`.
- **CI won't run, or will fail.** The new gates were added without widening the workflow's path filters, so PRs that only touch `evals/**` or the new `tools/` scripts never run them. Separately, this PR edits tracked `.claude/` files without regenerating `.claude/checksums.json`, so the new `gen-checksums.sh --check` gate should fail on this PR itself. That one is less certain, because the committed manifest isn't in the frozen snapshot.

**Smaller issues:**
- The run-level `--max-usd` cap doesn't count the cost of a retried first attempt, and it accepts `0.0`.
- `took-effect.sh` reports several rules as OK when `meta/pipeline.json` is corrupt, and it accepts a `running` status that its header doesn't list.
- `fresh-mount-proof.sh` ignores failed steps inside `run_step`.
- `check-manifest-paths.sh` flags non-ASCII paths as untracked because it doesn't use `-z`.
- Launcher failures (exit 125–127) are scored as agent errors instead of infrastructure errors.
- The price cache never persists, `pipeline-run.sh` breaks on jq 1.6, the snapshot index keys don't match the header, and missing option values in `spend.sh` exit 1 instead of 2.

The framework-side changes look fine. The model-config checksum matches its file, and `check-loa.sh`'s new `return 0` actually fixes an old early exit when drift was found.

About half the new bats files couldn't run here, because the snapshot is missing fixture run directories and parts of `.claude/`. `spend.bats` passes. One reviewer ran `pipeline-run.bats` on a copy patched past the jq 1.6 problem; four tests still failed and weren't traced, though the jq incompatibility is the likely cause. The rest of the findings come from reading the code plus small reproductions.
